page.layout: One page of text in a single column; running head at the top with the page number at its right; no marginal notes; no catchword or signature.

main_text.p: Regium est, bene facere, male audire, Illud faciam modo, hoc feram libens. (Deo gratias ago) patienter audire possum etiam quæ mihi affingunt Inimici deterrima. Spe-ro quoque me plus boni facturum, quam aut merentur Ifti, aut cupiunt.
Olim (credo) manifestum fiet, eos qui cætera mea Regna turbare cæperant, reos esse magnam partem etiam horridi istius in Hybernia cruoris, si non quâ primo fusi, at quâ tardè repressi.

Quem certè (quicquid ipsi dicant vel sentiant) non aliter accipio, quàm è venis meis hauftum tantum sanguinis, cum nemo prorsus, sat[?] scio, plus hâc effusione debilitetur. Quanquam verò infariata[?] sit hominum sævitia, spero Dei misericordiam Iustitiæ Ipsius aliquando dicturam, sufficit, & Civilium Bellorum Gladium in vaginam suam recondi iussuram, cum misericors Illius Iustitia non perniciem nostram velit, sed Medicinam: ut sit scelerum diminutio, non gentis excidium.

p.i: Præveniasnos (Deus Meus) repetitis tuis Misericordiis, quèus[?] Ego & Populus Meus fu-mus valde abusi, necsut[?] unquam restituantur, me-reri possumus.
Vides quanta inter Christianos immani-tas sub Religionis specie exercetur, quasi Chri-stians

page.notes: Running head and Greek title are set in Greek letters (ΕΙΚΩΝ ΒΑΣΙΛΙΚΗ); the scan shows them with Latin-looking capitals, transcribed as the Greek they spell. "infariata" (line 3 of the third paragraph) is uncertain; "sat" in "sat scio" is uncertain because the long s looks like f; "quèus" is doubtful (probably quibus); "necsut" is doubtful as printed. The last line of the page is cut off at the bottom edge, so the final word may be incomplete. Long s has been normalised to s throughout. The asterisk after "excidium" is an ornament and is not transcribed.
